newsitem.title: JAPAN: MITI mulls ways to rationalise Japan oil trade.
newsitem.headline: MITI mulls ways to rationalise Japan oil trade.

text.p: Japan's Trade Ministry said on Thursday it was considering various ways to enhance the transparency of the domestic oil product distribution system, in a bid to promote efficiency and competition.
An advisory committee to the Ministry of International Trade and Industry is looking at the following points:
-- Abolishing the need for newcomers to the gasoline retail market to acquire a certificate of supply from oil refiners.
-- Easing restrictions on the export of oil products.
-- Reviewing the system under which gasoline stations use trademarks.
-- Making clear the role of oil refiners, wholesalers and retailers.
-- Requiring full disclosure of oil product wholesale prices.
The committee is expected to come up with a final report by June or July, a Trade Ministry official said.
The need for certificates of supply has enabled oil refiners to keep a tight grip on gasoline stations.
By doing away with the certificates and revealing wholesale prices, MITI hopes to promote competition among gasoline stations and refiners, the official said.
